  "output_head": "# Fizzy

Guidance for AI coding agents working with this repository.

Fizzy is a kanban-style project management and issue tracker: cards move across columns on boards, with comments, mentions, and assignments.

## Deploy

Default branch: `main`

Self-hosted deploys run Kamal against `config/deploy.yml` — see `docs/kamal-deployment.md`.

## SaaS mode

For local agent work, `tmp/saas.txt` is the checkout-level SaaS switch used by `bin/setup`. When present, read `saas/AGENTS.md` before continuing. Otherwise, do not apply its instructions.

## Architecture Overview

### Multi-Tenancy (URL-Based)

Fizzy uses **URL path-based multi-tenancy**:
- Accounts have a unique decimal `external_account_id` used in URL prefixes
- URLs are prefixed: `/{account_id}/boards/...`
- Middleware (`AccountSlug::Extractor`) extracts the account ID from the URL and sets `Current.account`
- The slug is moved from `PATH_INFO` to `SCRIPT_NAME`, making Rails think it's "mounted" at that path
- Tenant-scoped domain records are account-isolated; global identity, session, and authentication records are exceptions
- Background jobs automatically serialize and restore account context

**Key insight**: This architecture allows multi-tenancy without subdomains or separate databases, making local development and testing simpler.

### Authentication & Authorization

Passwordless magic link authentication. A global `Identity` (email-based) can have `Users` in multiple Accounts, so an email is not a single account membership. Users have roles: owner, admin, member, system. Board-level access control via `Access` records.

### Entropy System

Cards automatically "postpone" (move to "not now") after inactivity:
- Account-level default entropy period
- Board-level entropy override
- Prevents endless todo lists from accumulating
- Configurable via Account/Board settings

### UUID Primary Keys

All tables use UUIDs (UUIDv7 format, base36-encoded as 25-char strings):
- Custom fixture UUID generation maintains deterministic ordering for tests
- Fixtures are always "older" than runtime records
- `.first`/`.last` work correctly in tests

### Background Jobs (Solid Queue)

Database-backed job queue (no Redis):
- Custom `FizzyActiveJobExtensions` prepended to ActiveJob
- Jobs automatically capture/restore `Current.account`
- Mission Control::Jobs for monitoring

Recurring tasks are declared in `config/recurring.yml`.

### Sharded Full-Text Search

Full-text search runs in the database, not Elasticsearch. On MySQL it is sharded 16 ways by CRC32 of the account ID (`Search::Record::Trilogy`); on SQLite it is a single FTS5 index (`Search::Record::SQLite`). Don't assume the sharded shape when working under SQLite. Models in `app/models/search/`.

### Imports and exports

Allow people to move between OSS and SAAS Fizzy instances:
- Exports/Imports can be written to/read from local or S3 storage depending on the config of the instance (both must be supported)
- Must be able to handle very large ZIP files (500+GB)
- Models in `app/models/account/data_transfer/`, `app/models/zip_file`

Passwordless magic link authentication. A global `Identity` (email-based) can have `Users` in multiple Accounts, so an email is not a single account membership. Users have roles: owner, admin, member, system. Board-level access control via `Access` records.

### Entropy System

Cards automatically "postpone" (move to "not now") after inactivity:
- Account-level default entropy period
- Board-level entropy override
- Prevents endless todo lists from accumulating
- Configurable via Account/Board settings

### UUID Primary Keys

All tables use UUIDs (UUIDv7 format, base36-encoded as 25-char strings):
- Custom fixture UUID generation maintains deterministic ordering for tests
- Fixtures are always "older" than runtime records
- `.first`/`.last` work correctly in tests

### Background Jobs (Solid Queue)

Database-backed job queue (no Redis):
- Custom `FizzyActiveJobExtensions` prepended to ActiveJob
- Jobs automatically capture/restore `Current.account`
- Mission Control::Jobs for monitoring

Recurring tasks are declared in `config/recurring.yml`.

### Sharded Full-Text Search

Full-text search runs in the database, not Elasticsearch. On MySQL it is sharded 16 ways by CRC32 of the account ID (`Search::Record::Trilogy`); on SQLite it is a single FTS5 index (`Search::Record::SQLite`). Don't assume the sharded shape when working under SQLite. Models in `app/models/search/`.

### Imports and exports

Allow people to move between OSS and SAAS Fizzy instances:
- Exports/Imports can be written to/read from local or S3 storage depending on the config of the instance (both must be supported)
- Must be able to handle very large ZIP files (500+GB)
- Models in `app/models/account/data_transfer/`, `app/models/zip_file`

## Coding style

Before editing or reviewing code, read STYLE.md.

# Fizzy SaaS

37signals' hosted Fizzy: billing, our production setup, our deploy destinations. Apply this only when SaaS mode is enabled — the root `AGENTS.md` has the check.

`bin/rails saas:enable` creates `tmp/saas.txt`; `bin/rails saas:disable` removes it. `Fizzy.saas?` also reads `SAAS` from the environment, where anything but `false` enables and `SAAS=false` forces off even with the file present (`lib/fizzy.rb`) — that path is for the production image and `bin/ci`, not for switching a checkout. Enabling swaps the bundle to `Gemfile.saas` and the default database adapter to MySQL, so it changes what every `bin/rails` and `bin/kamal` command does.

`README.md` covers the environments, Stripe, push credentials, and maintenance mode. What it doesn't say:

`saas:enable` is a prerequisite for deploying, not just for local development. Only under that flag does `bin/kamal` pass `-c` pointing at this gem's `config/deploy.yml`. Skip it and Kamal reads the root `config/deploy.yml` instead — the self-hosting example, which knows nothing about our destinations.

## Deploy

Pre-deploy: `bin/rails saas:enable`
Deploy: `bin/kamal deploy -d <destination>`
Destinations: production, staging, beta, beta1

One `saas/config/deploy.<destination>.yml` each — paths here are given from the repository root, because that's where you're working from, and `config/deploy.yml` at the root is the self-hosting example rather than ours. `beta` is a template requiring the `BETA_NUMBER` env var; `beta1` is the only numbered target that exists. The `saas/.kamal/secrets.beta2` through `saas/.kamal/secrets.beta4` symlinks are leftovers and don't make those destinations real.

The default branch stays in the root `AGENTS.md` — it describes the repository, not the hosted deployment.

# Style

We aim to write code that is a pleasure to read, and we have a lot of opinions about how to do it well. Writing great code is an essential part of our programming culture, and we deliberately set a high bar for every code change anyone contributes. We care about how code reads, how code looks, and how code makes you feel when you read it.

We love discussing code. If you have questions about how to write something, or if you detect some smell you are not quite sure how to solve, please ask away to other programmers. A Pull Request is a great way to do this.

When writing new code, unless you are very familiar with our approach, try to find similar code elsewhere to look for inspiration.

## Conditional returns

In general, we prefer to use expanded conditionals over guard clauses.

```ruby
# Bad
def todos_for_new_group
  ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]
  return [] unless ids
```

This is a Rails engine that [37signals](https://37signals.com/) bundles with [Fizzy](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy) to offer the hosted version at https://fizzy.do.

## Development

To make Fizzy run in SaaS mode, run this in the terminal:

```ruby
bin/rails saas:enable
```

To go back to open source mode:

```ruby
bin/rails saas:disable
```

Then you can do [Fizzy development as usual](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy).

## How to update Fizzy

After making changes to this gem, you need to update Fizzy to pick up the changes:

```ruby
BUNDLE_GEMFILE=Gemfile.saas bundle update --conservative fizzy-saas
```

## Working with Stripe

The first time, you need to:

1. Install Stripe CLI: https://stripe.com/docs/stripe-cli
2. Run `stripe login` and authorize the environment `37signals Development`

Then, for working on the Stripe integration locally, you need to run this script to start the tunneling and set the environment variables:

```sh
eval "$(BUNDLE_GEMFILE=Gemfile.saas bundle exec stripe-dev)"
bin/dev # You need to start the dev server in the same terminal session
```

This will ask for your 1password authorization to read and set the environment variables that Stripe needs.

### Stripe environments

* [Development](https://dashboard.stripe.com/acct_1SdTFtRus34tgjsJ/test/dashboard)
* [Staging](https://dashboard.stripe.com/acct_1SdTbuRvb8txnPBR/test/dashboard)
* [Production](https://dashboard.stripe.com/acct_1SNy97RwChFE4it8/dashboard)

## Working with Push Notifications

To test native push notifications (APNs and FCM) locally, start the dev server with the `--push` flag:

```sh
bin/dev --push
```

This will ask for your 1Password authorization to fetch the push credentials. Note that this loads the **production** APNs and FCM credentials into your environment.

## Environments

Fizzy is deployed with [Kamal](https://kamal-deploy.org/). You'll need to have the 1Password CLI set up in order to access the secrets that are used when deploying. Provided you have that, it should be as simple as `bin/kamal deploy` to the correct environment.

## Handbook

See the [Fizzy handbook](https://handbooks.37signals.works/18/fizzy) for runbooks and more.

### Production

- https://app.fizzy.do/

This environment uses a FlashBlade bucket for blob storage.

### Beta

Beta is primarily intended for testing product features. It uses the same production database and Active Storage configuration.

There is 1 beta environment:

- https://beta1.fizzy-beta.com

Deploy with: `bin/kamal deploy -d beta1`

### Staging

Staging is primarily intended for testing infrastructure changes. It uses production-like but separate database and Active Storage configurations.

- https://app.fizzy-staging.com/

## Maintenance mode

To take production offline for maintenance, run `kamal-proxy stop` on the load balancers via `knife ssh`:

```bash
knife ssh 'hostname:fizzy-lb-*' "sudo docker exec fizzy-load-balancer kamal-proxy stop fizzy --message='Sorry! Fizzy is undergoing some maintenance and will be back shortly.'"
```

Verify maintenance is enabled by visiting https://app.fizzy.do/.

To lift maintenance mode:

```bash
knife ssh 'hostname:fizzy-lb-*' 'sudo docker exec fizzy-load-balancer kamal-proxy resume fizzy'
```

## License

fizzy-saas is released under the [O'Saasy License](LICENSE.md).

module Fizzy
  class << self
    def saas?
      return @saas if defined?(@saas)
      @saas = !!(((ENV["SAAS"] || File.exist?(File.expand_path("../tmp/saas.txt", __dir__))) && ENV["SAAS"] != "false"))
    end

    def db_adapter
      @db_adapter ||= DbAdapter.new ENV.fetch("DATABASE_ADAPTER", saas? ? "mysql" : "sqlite")
    end

    def configure_bundle
      if saas?
        ENV["BUNDLE_GEMFILE"] = "Gemfile.saas"
      end
    end
  end

  class DbAdapter
    def initialize(name)
      @name = name.to_s
    end

    def to_s
      @name
    end

    # Not using inquiry so that it works before Rails env loads.
    def sqlite?
      @name == "sqlite"
    end
  end
end

First, I need to thoroughly understand how the SaaS module is *already* implemented. I'm going to pore over all the relevant files: the migrations, schemas, `engine.rb`, routes, models, controllers, views, and tests within `saas/`. I need to understand the architecture within that module. Beyond that, I need to see how the main application interacts with *this* SaaS component through hooks. I'm thinking: view partials, shared concerns, that `Fizzy.saas?` guard, storage limits, account settings, payment handling, and the admin interface. I need a holistic view of the interaction.

Specifically, I'll be meticulously examining the database schema and migration files within the `saas/db/` directory, including the `saas_schema.rb` and its SQLite variant, in case there are subtle differences between database implementations. I'll need to know those. The `saas/lib/fizzy/saas/engine.rb` file is key, of course, to understand the modular design. And of course, the `saas/lib/fizzy/saas.rb` file, and `saas/config/routes.rb` too. This is where the core logic and routing are defined. This is where I'll get to the heart of the matter. From there, I'll get a clear picture of its role in the system.

module Fizzy
  module Saas
    module Signup
      extend ActiveSupport::Concern

      included do
        attr_reader :queenbee_account
      end

      private
        def create_tenant
          @queenbee_account = Queenbee::Remote::Account.create!(queenbee_account_attributes)
          @queenbee_account.id.to_s
        end

        def handle_account_creation_error(error)
          @queenbee_account&.cancel
        end

        def queenbee_account_attributes

            attributes[:name]           = generate_account_name
            attributes[:owner_name]     = full_name
            attributes[:owner_email]    = email_address

            attributes[:trial]          = true
            attributes[:subscription]   = subscription_attributes
            attributes[:remote_request] = request_attributes

            # # TODO: Terms of Service
            # attributes[:terms_of_service] = true

            # We've confirmed the email
            attributes[:auto_allow]     = true

            # Tell Queenbee to skip the request to create a local account. We've created it ourselves.
            attributes[:skip_remote]    = true
          end
        end
    end
  end

module Account::StorageLimited
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  DEFAULT_STORAGE_LIMIT = 1.gigabyte
  NEAR_STORAGE_LIMIT_THRESHOLD = 500.megabytes

  included do
    has_one :storage_exception
  end

  def storage_limit
    storage_exception&.bytes_allowed || DEFAULT_STORAGE_LIMIT
  end

  def exceeding_storage_limit?
    bytes_used > storage_limit
  end

  def nearing_storage_limit?
    !exceeding_storage_limit? && bytes_used > storage_limit - NEAR_STORAGE_LIMIT_THRESHOLD
  end

  def add_storage_exception(bytes)
    if storage_exception
      storage_exception.update!(bytes_allowed: bytes)
    else
      create_storage_exception!(bytes_allowed: bytes)
    end
  end
end

require "test_helper"

class Account::StorageExceptionTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "storage limit returns default when no exception exists" do
    assert_equal Account::StorageLimited::DEFAULT_STORAGE_LIMIT, accounts(:initech).storage_limit
  end

  test "storage limit returns exception value when one exists" do
    account = accounts(:initech)
    account.add_storage_exception(5.gigabytes)

    assert_equal 5.gigabytes, account.storage_limit
  end

  test "add storage exception creates a new record" do
    account = accounts(:initech)

    assert_difference -> { Account::StorageException.count } do
      account.add_storage_exception(2.gigabytes)
    end

    assert_equal 2.gigabytes, account.storage_exception.bytes_allowed
  end

  test "add storage exception updates existing record" do
    account = accounts(:initech)
    account.add_storage_exception(2.gigabytes)

    assert_no_difference -> { Account::StorageException.count } do
      account.add_storage_exception(10.gigabytes)
    end

    assert_equal 10.gigabytes, account.storage_exception.reload.bytes_allowed
  end

  test "exceeding storage limit respects exception" do
    account = accounts(:initech)
    Account.any_instance.stubs(:bytes_used).returns(2.gigabytes)

    assert account.exceeding_storage_limit?

    account.add_storage_exception(5.gigabytes)

    assert_not account.exceeding_storage_limit?
  end
end

require "test_helper"
require "queenbee/testing/client"

class Account::QueenbeeIntegrationTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  include Queenbee::Testing::Client

  # Fizzy creates accounts via its own Signup flow (Fizzy → Queenbee),
  # not via Queenbee pushing to Fizzy, so create_with_dependents is N/A.
  undef_method :test_client_class_should_respond_to_create_with_dependents

  setup do
    @account = accounts(:"37s")
  end

  test "find_by_queenbee_id looks up by external_account_id" do
    assert_equal @account, Account.find_by_queenbee_id(@account.external_account_id)
  end

  test "queenbee_id returns external_account_id" do
    assert_equal @account.external_account_id, @account.queenbee_id
  end

  test "cancel! creates cancellation attributed to system user" do
    @account.cancel!

    assert @account.cancelled?
    assert_equal @account.system_user, @account.cancellation.initiated_by
  end

  test "cancel! is idempotent" do
    @account.cancel!
    assert_no_difference -> { Account::Cancellation.count } do
      @account.cancel!
    end
  end

  test "cancel and reactivate round-trips" do
    @account.cancel!
    assert_not @account.active?

    @account.reactivate!
    @account.reload
    assert @account.active?
  end

  test "deactivate! cancels the account" do
    @account.deactivate!
    assert @account.cancelled?
  end

  test "owner_name and owner_email from account owner" do
    assert_equal users(:jason).name, @account.owner_name
    assert_equal "jason@37signals.com", @account.owner_email
  end

  test "comped= is a no-op" do
    @account.comped = true
    assert_not @account.comped?
  end

  test "transferred_ownership! raises NotImplementedError" do
    assert_raises(NotImplementedError) { @account.transferred_ownership! }
  end

  test "qb_serializable_hash includes queenbee_id and subscription" do
    hash = @account.qb_serializable_hash
    assert_equal @account.external_account_id, hash[:id]
    assert_equal({ quantity: 1 }, hash[:subscription])
  end
end

class Card::StorageLimited::CreationTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest

    sign_in_as :mike

    Account.any_instance.stubs(:bytes_used).returns(1.gigabyte + 1)

    assert_no_difference -> { Card.count } do
      post board_cards_path(boards(:miltons_wish_list), script_name: accounts(:initech).slug),

        as: :json
    end

    assert_response :forbidden

    sign_in_as :mike

    Account.any_instance.stubs(:bytes_used).returns(1.gigabyte + 1)
    accounts(:initech).update_column(:cards_count, 100)
    boards(:miltons_wish_list).cards.drafted.where(creator: users(:mike)).destroy_all

    assert_difference -> { Card.count } do
      post board_cards_path(boards(:miltons_wish_list), script_name: accounts(:initech).slug)

    def assign_number

module Queenbee
  singleton_class.attr_accessor :host_app

  # no remote counterpart to serve, so there is nothing to draw.
  def self.routes(mapper)
  end

    singleton_class.attr_accessor :token
  end

    end
  end

    singleton_class.attr_accessor :short_names

    def self.property(name, value)
      properties[name] = value
      define_method(name) { value }
      define_singleton_method(name) { value }
    end

      @properties ||= superclass.respond_to?(:properties) ? superclass.properties.dup : {}

        attributes.key?(name) ? attributes[name] : super
      end

      def respond_to_missing?(name, include_private = false)
        attributes.key?(name) || super

    def generate_fixture_uuid(label)
      # Generate deterministic UUIDv7 for fixtures that sorts by fixture ID
      # This allows .first/.last to work as expected in tests
      # Use the same CRC32 algorithm as Rails' default fixture ID generation
      # so that UUIDs sort in the same order as integer IDs
      fixture_int = Zlib.crc32("fixtures/#{label}") % (2**30 - 1)

      # Translate the deterministic order into times in the past, so that records
      # created during test runs are also always newer than the fixtures.
      base_time = Time.utc(2024, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)
      timestamp = base_time + (fixture_int / 1000.0)

      uuid_v7_with_timestamp(timestamp, label)
    end

    def uuid_v7_with_timestamp(time, seed_string)
      # Generate UUIDv7 with custom timestamp and deterministic random bits
      # Format: 48-bit timestamp_ms | 12-bit sub_ms_precision | 4-bit version | 62-bit random

      time_ms = time.to_f * 1000
      timestamp_ms = time_ms.to_i

      # 48-bit timestamp (milliseconds since epoch)
      bytes = []
      bytes[0] = (timestamp_ms >> 40) & 0xff
      bytes[1] = (timestamp_ms >> 32) & 0xff
      bytes[2] = (timestamp_ms >> 24) & 0xff
      bytes[3] = (timestamp_ms >> 16) & 0xff
      bytes[4] = (timestamp_ms >> 8) & 0xff
      bytes[5] = timestamp_ms & 0xff

      # Use the 12-bit rand_a field for sub-millisecond precision
      # Extract fractional milliseconds and convert to 12-bit value (0-4095)
      # This gives us ~0.244 microsecond precision
      frac_ms = time_ms - timestamp_ms
      sub_ms_precision = (frac_ms * 4096).to_i & 0xfff

      # Derive deterministic "random" bits from seed_string for the remaining random bits
      hash = Digest::MD5.hexdigest(seed_string)

      # 12-bit sub-ms precision + 4-bit version (0111 for v7)
      bytes[6] = ((sub_ms_precision >> 8) & 0x0f) | 0x70  # version 7
      bytes[7] = sub_ms_precision & 0xff

      # 2-bit variant (10) + 62-bit random
      rand_b = hash[3...19].to_i(16) & ((2**62) - 1)
      bytes[8] = ((rand_b >> 56) & 0x3f) | 0x80  # variant 10
      bytes[9] = (rand_b >> 48) & 0xff
      bytes[10] = (rand_b >> 40) & 0xff
      bytes[11] = (rand_b >> 32) & 0xff
      bytes[12] = (rand_b >> 24) & 0xff
      bytes[13] = (rand_b >> 16) & 0xff
      bytes[14] = (rand_b >> 8) & 0xff
      bytes[15] = rand_b & 0xff

      # Format as UUID string and convert to base36 (25 chars)
      uuid = "%02x%02x%02x%02x-%02x%02x-%02x%02x-%02x%02x-%02x%02x%02x%02x%02x%02x" % bytes

    def generate_fixture_uuid(label)
      # Generate deterministic UUIDv7 for fixtures that sorts by fixture ID
      # This allows .first/.last to work as expected in tests
      # Use the same CRC32 algorithm as Rails' default fixture ID generation
      # so that UUIDs sort in the same order as integer IDs
      fixture_int = Zlib.crc32("fixtures/#{label}") % (2**30 - 1)

      # Translate the deterministic order into times in the past, so that records
      # created during test runs are also always newer than the fixtures.
      base_time = Time.utc(2024, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)
      timestamp = base_time + (fixture_int / 1000.0)

      uuid_v7_with_timestamp(timestamp, label)
    end

    def uuid_v7_with_timestamp(time, seed_string)
      # Generate UUIDv7 with custom timestamp and deterministic random bits
      # Format: 48-bit timestamp_ms | 12-bit sub_ms_precision | 4-bit version | 62-bit random

      time_ms = time.to_f * 1000
      timestamp_ms = time_ms.to_i

      # 48-bit timestamp (milliseconds since epoch)
      bytes = []
      bytes[0] = (timestamp_ms >> 40) & 0xff
      bytes[1] = (timestamp_ms >> 32) & 0xff
      bytes[2] = (timestamp_ms >> 24) & 0xff
      bytes[3] = (timestamp_ms >> 16) & 0xff
      bytes[4] = (timestamp_ms >> 8) & 0xff
      bytes[5] = timestamp_ms & 0xff

      # Use the 12-bit rand_a field for sub-millisecond precision
      # Extract fractional milliseconds and convert to 12-bit value (0-4095)
      # This gives us ~0.244 microsecond precision
      frac_ms = time_ms - timestamp_ms
      sub_ms_precision = (frac_ms * 4096).to_i & 0xfff

      # Derive deterministic "random" bits from seed_string for the remaining random bits
      hash = Digest::MD5.hexdigest(seed_string)

      # 12-bit sub-ms precision + 4-bit version (0111 for v7)
      bytes[6] = ((sub_ms_precision >> 8) & 0x0f) | 0x70  # version 7
      bytes[7] = sub_ms_precision & 0xff

      # 2-bit variant (10) + 62-bit random
      rand_b = hash[3...19].to_i(16) & ((2**62) - 1)
      bytes[8] = ((rand_b >> 56) & 0x3f) | 0x80  # variant 10
      bytes[9] = (rand_b >> 48) & 0xff
      bytes[10] = (rand_b >> 40) & 0xff
      bytes[11] = (rand_b >> 32) & 0xff
      bytes[12] = (rand_b >> 24) & 0xff
      bytes[13] = (rand_b >> 16) & 0xff
      bytes[14] = (rand_b >> 8) & 0xff
      bytes[15] = rand_b & 0xff

      # Format as UUID string and convert to base36 (25 chars)
      uuid = "%02x%02x%02x%02x-%02x%02x-%02x%02x-%02x%02x-%02x%02x%02x%02x%02x%02x" % bytes

require "test_helper"

class Account::CancellableTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    @account = accounts(:"37s")
    @user = users(:david)
  end

  test "cancel" do
    assert_difference -> { Account::Cancellation.count }, 1 do
      assert_enqueued_with(job: ActionMailer::MailDeliveryJob) do
        @account.cancel(initiated_by: @user)
      end
    end

    assert @account.cancelled?
    assert_equal @user, @account.cancellation.initiated_by
  end

  test "cancel does nothing if already cancelled" do
    @account.cancel(initiated_by: @user)

    assert_no_changes -> { @account.cancellation.reload.created_at } do
      @account.cancel(initiated_by: @user)
    end
  end

  test "cancel does nothing when in single-tenant mode" do
    Account.stubs(:accepting_signups?).returns(false)

    assert_no_difference -> { Account::Cancellation.count } do
      @account.cancel(initiated_by: @user)
    end

    assert_not @account.cancelled?
  end

  test "cancelled? returns true when cancellation exists" do
    assert_not @account.cancelled?

    @account.cancel(initiated_by: @user)

    assert @account.cancelled?
  end

  test "reactivate" do
    @account.cancel(initiated_by: @user)

    assert @account.cancelled?

    @account.reactivate
    @account.reload

    assert_not @account.cancelled?
    assert_nil @account.cancellation
  end

  test "reactivate does nothing if not cancelled" do
    assert_not @account.cancelled?

    assert_nothing_raised do
      @account.reactivate
    end

require "test_helper"

class Account::CancellableTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    @account = accounts(:"37s")
    @user = users(:david)
  end

  test "cancel" do
    assert_difference -> { Account::Cancellation.count }, 1 do
      assert_enqueued_with(job: ActionMailer::MailDeliveryJob) do
        @account.cancel(initiated_by: @user)
      end
    end

    assert @account.cancelled?
    assert_equal @user, @account.cancellation.initiated_by
  end

  test "cancel does nothing if already cancelled" do
    @account.cancel(initiated_by: @user)

    assert_no_changes -> { @account.cancellation.reload.created_at } do
      @account.cancel(initiated_by: @user)
    end
  end

  test "cancel does nothing when in single-tenant mode" do
    Account.stubs(:accepting_signups?).returns(false)

    assert_no_difference -> { Account::Cancellation.count } do
      @account.cancel(initiated_by: @user)
    end

    assert_not @account.cancelled?
  end

  test "cancelled? returns true when cancellation exists" do
    assert_not @account.cancelled?

    @account.cancel(initiated_by: @user)

    assert @account.cancelled?
  end

  test "reactivate" do
    @account.cancel(initiated_by: @user)

    assert @account.cancelled?

    @account.reactivate
    @account.reload

    assert_not @account.cancelled?
    assert_nil @account.cancellation
  end

  test "reactivate does nothing if not cancelled" do
    assert_not @account.cancelled?

    assert_nothing_raised do
      @account.reactivate
    end

    assert_not @account.cancelled?
  end

  test "active scope excludes cancelled accounts" do
    account2 = accounts(:initech)

    initial_active_count = Account.active.count

    @account.cancel(initiated_by: @user)

    assert_equal initial_active_count - 1, Account.active.count
    assert_not_includes Account.active, @account
    assert_includes Account.active, account2
  end
end

But, let's slow down. I'm seeing `cards_count` vs. the card count method, and the interaction with tests. Specifically, I'm thinking about that line in the test `saas/test/controllers/card/storage_limited/creation_test.rb`, which updates the `cards_count` column. Why is that there? Is that test relying on `cards_count` being *the* source of truth for card limits?

I need to confirm `cards_count` is being correctly set for each card's number. So looking into it, `Card#assign_number` seems to be the culprit. It increments `account.cards_count` *before* a card is published, which means drafts increment the count. The card number is generated by this increment, so the user never sees this logic. Okay, now I'm starting to see why the test works the way it does.

Now, let's talk boundaries! A user is limited to a card count, and the limit logic relies on `cards_count`.  Let's say `plan.card_limit` is 1000.  If we're at 950 cards, we'll see "50 cards left".  But, what does this mean in practice at the limit? We need to verify what happens when they hit 1000 cards. What happens when the user tries to create a card after the limit?

The critical part of this is the distinction between creating a *draft* card (via UI) vs. publishing one (API call or 'Create' button). Creating a draft *always* increments the `cards_count` column. When a user clicks "Add a card" in the UI, we increment the account's card count. This will be different from creating an API card, because in that case, the count will increment when the card is in a published status.

Here is the thing to carefully understand: what if the admin enters the limit value into the field?

Let's trace:

If a plan has a limit of 1000 cards:

1.  A user can create drafts up until that limit, but can no longer publish or create via API because `cards_count >= plan.card_limit` will refuse new cards.
2.  If an admin enters "1000" in the override field, we need to carefully test that this correctly limits the number of cards.

If we're using `>=` for exceeding the card limit and `overridden_limits&.card_count || cards_count`:

1.  The test will set `account.update_column(:cards_count, 1000)` and, from there, cannot publish or create any new card via the API. HTML creates should work, but they should redirect to the draft page.
2.  However, let's say a test is written where `cards_count = 950` then is set and is working as expected.

I also need to verify that we're counting published cards only, unless the override has been used!

Now, the BIG question. Why is `cards_count` set to 100 in the test? The `creation_test.rb` is testing what happens when the storage limits have been exceeded. messages.thinking:
**Deep Dive into Card Limits and Staff Access**

Okay, here's the deal. I've been dissecting how card limits work in this system, especially in the context of free accounts and staff users. The core issue was the discrepancy between the way we track card counts (`cards_count`) and what's actually published (`cards.published.count`), and how it interacts with the admin override form, which can stubs card limits, storage limits, and staff status.

First, I had to untangle `cards_count` from `cards.published.count`. `cards_count` is the monotonically increasing card counter; it's the total number ever created (like an ever-increasing ID) and is super fast, because it's stored directly in the `accounts` table. It's *not* a real-time count of published cards. This is crucial because it lets us easily stub the total count, which can be *really* fast, rather than creating hundreds of actual card records, especially in tests.

The goal is to provide a consistent and expected behavior and UI. Here's what needs to happen:

*   **Model Logic:** We need to keep the model logic very clean. `cards_used` (i.e., `overridden_limits&.card_count || cards_count`) is *the* metric to use for limits. This enables admins to change card limits at the model level (e.g., `account.update!(cards_count: 1000)`), the admin override form, or through direct overrides. The important thing is that `Card#assign_number` *must* increment the real `accounts.cards_count`, so real card creation works without hitting any overrides or stubs. The same applies for all storage limit calculations.

*   **Controller Enforcement:** The rule is this: free accounts can *draft* cards even if they're over the limit, but publishing and API-based card creation MUST be refused. The `CardsController#create` (JSON) and `Cards::PublishesController#create` should both return a `403 Forbidden` when the card limit is reached. The test suites already establish that convention.

*   **`staff?` & Limits:** Now, here's where it got tricky. We *do not* want staff users to bypass the card limits. These *must* be enforced, even for staff, when testing with the override forms. This is really important. The original design was for storage limits *only* to have a staff bypass (with the `!Current.identity.staff?` clause). We need to verify that we are not breaking existing storage limit tests, or introducing any new issues, so `!Current.identity.staff?` *only* applies to storage limits. In the `saas/test/` suite, we're explicitly testing "staff can see the UI," so we must keep it that way.

*   **Testing and Fixtures:** The fixtures already define staff members, and existing tests rely on those staff members being subject to override limit and storage allowances. This is what it all hinges on. We must keep those existing tests running by correctly using the override forms to test UI limits.

*   **UI/UX:** The "Upgrade" pitch in the UI needs to be triggered consistently. If `cards_used >= plan.card_limit`, we show it. This must also work for an individual card. When cards are at or over the limit, the HTML draft card view should show an upgrade pitch, *not* create buttons. This matches how the API will behave. Furthermore, we must retain the UI message on a warning countdown. For example, if a user's free account can have a maximum of 1,000 cards, and a staff user adds a limit override in the admin, the "upgrade" pitch should appear after those limits are at or exceed capacity, and the countdown warnings must still appear.

This should allow testing of all UI limit behaviors. This approach ensures that everything, from model calculations to controller enforcement to the UI, works consistently and as expected. It also keeps all existing tests running. The bottom line is consistency with the user interface and behavior. This approach ensures a consistent experience with the system in terms of storage limit exceptions, card limit warnings, and admin overrides.

**Stripe v18.4.2 Analysis: Data Field Shape Differences & Robust Webhook Handling**

Okay, this is exciting! I'm taking a look at Stripe v18.4.2 and need to get a clear picture of how they're representing `Stripe::Event` and `Stripe::Subscription` fields, particularly around how `current_period_end` is structured. The key here is the difference between Stripe API versions from before and after March 31, 2025. I need to make sure I completely understand how these payloads are shaped in order to build robust webhook handling!

The API change is the kicker: in the 2025-03-31+ API, `current_period_end` is nested deeper, moving to `items.data[0].current_period_end`. Older webhook payloads, however, had that data right on the subscription object itself.

My goal is to craft webhook processing that's completely backward-compatible. If I have a webhook handler that reads `current_period_end = stripe_subscription["current_period_end"] || stripe_subscription.dig("items", "data", 0, "current_period_end")`, that handles *both* the old and the new shapes automatically! That's the ideal approach.

I also need to verify how `plan_key` or `price_id` is extracted from the subscription object. Consider this extractor: `price_id = stripe_subscription.dig("items", "data", 0, "price", "id") || stripe_subscription.dig("items", "data", 0, "plan", "id") || stripe_subscription.dig("plan", "id")`. Talk about robust! Whether a modern Stripe webhook or some legacy test fixture sends `items: { data: [ { price: { id: "price_..." } } ] }`, or `items: { data: [ { plan: { id: "price_..." } } ] }` or `plan: { id: "price_..." }` it still pulls the right `price_id`. I love that level of flexibility.

Finally, I need to test that `Stripe::StripeObject`'s hash-like access (`dig` and `[]`) in Ruby is working as expected with Stripe 18.4.2. I'm going to run some tests with `Stripe::Event.construct_from(...)` right away. Let's make sure there are no surprises with the dig/array accessors.

messages.thinking:
**Fizzy Toggle and Database Considerations**

Alright, let's break this down. My initial focus is on the UI elements within Fizzy, specifically the toggles for "Comp"/"Uncomp" and the "Reset" button related to overrides. The logic is fairly straightforward for "Comp"/"Uncomp": it should toggle based on the `@account.comped?` state. If the account is comped, the UI shows "Uncomp"; otherwise, it shows "Comp". This aligns perfectly with a clear, user-friendly interaction.

The "Reset" button's visibility and behavior are where the deeper thought is. The core question is whether to *always* render the "Reset" button or only render it when an override exists (`@account.overridden_limits&.persisted?`). My instinct leans towards always showing the button. Even if there's no override, clicking "Reset" should be safe and idempotent, simply destroying the `overridden_limits` if it exists (which is a no-op if it doesn't). This approach makes the UI more predictable, prevents potentially failing integration tests that check for button presence, and aligns with the prompt's description of the UI elements. The user should expect to see the button and clicking it does what's expected.

Now, let's touch upon the database interaction. My primary concern is cross-database `includes` for listing accounts in the admin interface. I remember the `Account` model is in the *primary* database, while `Subscription`, `BillingWaiver`, and `OverriddenLimits` reside in the *saas* database. I'm relieved to discover that `includes` (specifically `preload`) should gracefully handle these cross-database relationships in Rails 8.2, executing separate queries on each database. It’s crucial that we *always* use `includes` or `preload` here, and never `joins` or `eager_load`, which would likely result in errors. I'll test it directly with SQLite where the database files are separate to ensure this behaves as expected. This will be an important pattern to watch for elsewhere.

module PaginationHelper
  def pagination_frame_tag(namespace, page, data: {}, **attributes, &)
    turbo_frame_tag pagination_frame_id_for(namespace, page.number), data: { timeline_target: "frame", **data }, role: "presentation", **attributes, &
  end

  def link_to_next_page(namespace, page, activate_when_observed: false, label: default_pagination_label(activate_when_observed), data: {}, **attributes)
    if page.before_last? && !params[:previous]
      attributes[:class] = class_names(attributes[:class], "btn txt-small center-block center": !activate_when_observed)
      pagination_link(namespace, page.number + 1, label: label, activate_when_observed: activate_when_observed, data: data, **attributes)
    end
  end

  def pagination_link(namespace, page_number, activate_when_observed: false, label: default_pagination_label(activate_when_observed), url_params: {}, data: {}, **attributes)
    link_to label, url_for(params.permit!.to_h.merge(page: page_number, **url_params)),
      "aria-label": "Load page #{page_number}",
      id: "#{namespace}-pagination-link-#{page_number}",
      class: class_names(attributes.delete(:class), "pagination-link", { "pagination-link--active-when-observed" => activate_when_observed }),
      data: {
        frame: pagination_frame_id_for(namespace, page_number),
        pagination_target: "paginationLink",
        action: ("click->pagination#loadPage:prevent" unless activate_when_observed),
        **data
      },
      **attributes
  end

  def pagination_frame_id_for(namespace, page_number)
    "#{namespace}-pagination-contents-#{page_number}"
  end

  def with_manual_pagination(name, page, **properties)
    pagination_list name, **properties do
      concat(pagination_frame_tag(name, page) do
        yield
        concat link_to_next_page(name, page)
      end)
    end
  end

  def with_automatic_pagination(name, page, **properties)
    pagination_list name, paginate_on_scroll: true, **properties do
      concat(pagination_frame_tag(name, page) do
        yield
        concat link_to_next_page(name, page, activate_when_observed: true)
      end)
    end
  end

  def day_timeline_pagination_frame_tag(day_timeline, &)
    turbo_frame_tag day_timeline_pagination_frame_id_for(day_timeline.day), data: { timeline_target: "frame" }, role: "presentation", refresh: :morph, &
  end

  def day_timeline_pagination_frame_id_for(day)
    "day-timeline-pagination-contents-#{day.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")}"
  end

  def day_timeline_pagination_link(day_timeline, filter)
    if day_timeline.next_day
      link_to "Load more…", events_days_path(day: day_timeline.next_day.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"), **filter.as_params),
        class: "day-timeline-pagination-link", data: { frame: day_timeline_pagination_frame_id_for(day_timeline.next_day), pagination_target: "paginationLink" }
    end
  end

  private
    def pagination_list(name, tag_element: :div, paginate_on_scroll: false, **properties, &block)
      classes = properties.delete(:class)
      properties[:id] ||= "#{name}-pagination-list"
      tag.public_send tag_element,
        class: token_list(name, "display-contents", classes),
        data: { controller: "pagination", pagination_paginate_on_intersection_value: paginate_on_scroll },
        **properties,
        &block
    end

    def default_pagination_label(activate_when_observed)
      "Load more…"
    end
end

**Step 2: Core Billing Models, Concerns, Job, and Engine Wiring - My Thoughts**

Alright, the schemas are synced, and it's time to build out the core billing logic. I'm going to meticulously review each file, ensuring strict adherence to our coding style and Omakase Rails principles. Method ordering, invocation order, clean conditionals, visibility modifiers, no unnecessary bangs, and thin controllers are all paramount here.

I'm starting with `Plan`. This file defines our various pricing tiers: free, monthly, and a monthly-plus with extra storage. The `PLANS` hash is elegant, storing all the key attributes for each plan. I like the use of `freeze` to prevent accidental modification. I'll make sure to get the accessors and methods right: class, public, then private.

Next, I'll move on to `Account::BillingWaiver`. This is straightforward; a simple `belongs_to` association to the `account` and a uniqueness validation.

`Account::OverriddenLimits` is next. This model allows overriding card and storage limits. The validations are important, ensuring that the overrides are integer values and non-negative.

Now, let's analyze `Account::Subscription`. This file is crucial because it's where we handle Stripe webhook events. I'm going to dive deep into every possible webhook scenario.

I'll map out all of the Stripe events:
-   `checkout.session.completed`: This is where a new subscription starts. I need to make sure I'm correctly extracting the account ID, plan key, and customer ID from the session and properly linking the subscription to the account.
-   `customer.subscription.created` / `customer.subscription.updated`: These events signify subscription changes. I need to handle updates to the subscription, including plan changes, status changes, and ensuring the correct subscription is linked to the correct account and handling stale old subscriptions.
-   `customer.subscription.deleted`: This is where a subscription is canceled. I will update the account's subscription appropriately, and guard against stale deletions.
-   `invoice.upcoming`, `invoice.payment_succeeded`, `invoice.paid`, `invoice.payment_failed`: Handling invoices. Especially, I will need to be careful with the nuances of these events, particularly around failures and how Stripe manages retries.

I'll be thorough to handle different object shapes for `subscription_obj` (string ID vs hash) and ensure resilience. I'll be sure to handle both API versions ( <= 2024 and >= 2025).

The `sync_from_stripe` method is complex but essential. I need to be meticulously careful to extract, apply, and calculate all the attributes correctly:
*   subscription ID
*   customer ID
*   status
*   plan (handling both `price_id`, `plan.id`, and `metadata.plan_key`)
*   period end
*   cancellation
*   amount due

It's clear, robust, and handles edge cases beautifully! I like the fact that this processing is idempotent and doesn't make any external calls.

`Account::CancelSubscriptionJob` is a simple job to handle the cancellation of subscriptions. Straightforward, it just calls `cancel_now`.

Now on to `Account::Billing`. This is where all the business logic lives.

I need to make sure that I understand and implement the methods to find the plan, check paid status, manage comps, override limits, and create Stripe checkout sessions. I'll need to pay careful attention to the logic to determine which plan an account is on (subscription, comped, or free). The comp logic is essential for our special cases, and the override_limits method needs to be robust, accounting for `nil`, `""` and the case of zero values. The checkout session creation needs to be flawless, including handling the customer ID, mode, line items, success/cancel URLs, client reference, and metadata. Also, I need to make sure to create the billing portal sessions correctly. The private `find_or_create_stripe_customer_id` helper looks very clean. Finally, the subscription cancellation also looks simple.

`Account::StorageLimited` is straightforward - this file is responsible for ensuring the storage limits can be changed by a storage exception.

Finally, I'm removing the placeholder methods from `Account::QueenbeeIntegration`, keeping only the `comped=` no-op.

Now, it's time to build these files. I'm confident that these models and jobs cover all the billing scenarios effectively and in a way that aligns with our architecture.

class Plan
  PLANS = {
    free_v1: {
      name: "Free",
      price: 0,
      card_limit: 1_000,
      storage_limit: 1.gigabyte,
      stripe_price_id_env: nil
    },
    monthly_v1: {
      name: "Unlimited",
      price: 20,
      card_limit: Float::INFINITY,
      storage_limit: 5.gigabytes,
      stripe_price_id_env: "STRIPE_MONTHLY_V1_PRICE_ID"
    },
    monthly_extra_storage_v1: {
      name: "Unlimited+",
      price: 25,
      card_limit: Float::INFINITY,
      storage_limit: 500.gigabytes,
      stripe_price_id_env: "STRIPE_MONTHLY_EXTRA_STORAGE_V1_PRICE_ID"
    }
  }.freeze

  attr_reader :key, :name, :price, :card_limit, :storage_limit

  class << self
    def all
      @all ||= PLANS.map { |key, properties| new(key: key, **properties) }
    end

    def paid_plans
      all.select(&:paid?)
    end

    def free
      find(:free_v1)
    end

    def unlimited
      find(:monthly_v1)
    end
    alias paid unlimited

    def unlimited_plus
      find(:monthly_extra_storage_v1)
    end

    def find(key)
      if key.present?
        all.find { |plan| plan.key == key.to_sym }
      end
    end

    def find_by_price_id(price_id)
      if price_id.present?
        paid_plans.find { |plan| plan.stripe_price_id == price_id }
      end
    end
  end

  def initialize(key:, name:, price:, card_limit:, storage_limit:, stripe_price_id_env:)
    @key = key.to_sym
    @name = name
    @price = price
    @card_limit = card_limit
    @storage_limit = storage_limit
    @stripe_price_id_env = stripe_price_id_env
  end

  def stripe_price_id
    ENV[@stripe_price_id_env].presence if @stripe_price_id_env
  end

  def free?
    price.zero?
  end

  def paid?
    !free?
  end

  def limit_cards?
    card_limit.finite?
  end

  def unlimited_cards?
    card_limit.infinite?
  end

  def ==(other)
    other.is_a?(Plan) && key == other.key
  end
  alias eql? ==

  def hash
    key.hash
  end

  def to_s
    name
  end
end
EOF

cat <<'EOF' > saas/app/models/account/subscription.rb
class Account::Subscription < SaasRecord
  belongs_to :account

  enum :status, %w[ active past_due unpaid canceled incomplete incomplete_expired trialing paused ].index_by(&:itself)

  validates :account_id, uniqueness: true
  validates :stripe_customer_id, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validates :stripe_subscription_id, uniqueness: true, allow_nil: true
  validates :plan_key, inclusion: { in: Plan::PLANS.keys.map(&:to_s) }, allow_nil: true

  class << self
    def process_stripe_event(event)
      case event.type
      when "checkout.session.completed"
        process_checkout_session_completed(event.data.object)
      when "customer.subscription.created", "customer.subscription.updated"
        process_subscription_changed(event.data.object)
      when "customer.subscription.deleted"
        process_subscription_deleted(event.data.object)
      when "invoice.upcoming"
        process_invoice_upcoming(event.data.object)
      end
    end

    private
      def process_checkout_session_completed(session)
        hash = symbolize(session)
        return if hash[:mode].present? && hash[:mode] != "subscription"

        customer_id = extract_id(hash[:customer])
        subscription_data = hash[:subscription]
        subscription_id = extract_id(subscription_data)
        account_id = hash.dig(:metadata, :account_id) || hash[:client_reference_id]
        plan_key = hash.dig(:metadata, :plan_key)

        record = find_or_initialize_for_stripe(
          stripe_customer_id: customer_id,
          stripe_subscription_id: subscription_id,
          account_id: account_id
        )
        return unless record

        if subscription_data.is_a?(Hash) || subscription_data.is_a?(Stripe::StripeObject)
          record.sync_from_stripe(subscription_data)
        else
          attributes = {}
          attributes[:stripe_customer_id] = customer_id if customer_id.present?
          attributes[:stripe_subscription_id] = subscription_id if subscription_id.present?
          attributes[:plan_key] = plan_key if Plan.find(plan_key)&.paid?

          if (record.status.blank? || record.incomplete? || record.canceled?) && hash[:payment_status] != "unpaid"
            attributes[:status] = "active"
          end

          record.update!(attributes) if attributes.any?
        end
      end

      def process_subscription_changed(stripe_subscription)
        hash = symbolize(stripe_subscription)
        subscription_id = hash[:id]
        customer_id = extract_id(hash[:customer])
        account_id = hash.dig(:metadata, :account_id)

        record = find_or_initialize_for_stripe(
          stripe_customer_id: customer_id,
          stripe_subscription_id: subscription_id,
          account_id: account_id
        )
        return unless record

        if stale_subscription_event?(record, subscription_id, hash[:status])
          return
        end

        record.sync_from_stripe(hash)
      end

      def process_subscription_deleted(stripe_subscription)
        hash = symbolize(stripe_subscription)
        subscription_id = hash[:id]
        customer_id = extract_id(hash[:customer])

        record = find_by(stripe_subscription_id: subscription_id) || find_by(stripe_customer_id: customer_id)
        return unless record

        if record.stripe_subscription_id.present? && record.stripe_subscription_id != subscription_id
          return
        end

        record.sync_from_stripe(hash, force_status: "canceled")
      end

      def process_invoice_upcoming(invoice)
        hash = symbolize(invoice)
        subscription_id = extract_id(hash[:subscription]) ||
          extract_id(hash.dig(:parent, :subscription_details, :subscription))
        customer_id = extract_id(hash[:customer])

        record = (find_by(stripe_subscription_id: subscription_id) if subscription_id.present?) ||
          (find_by(stripe_customer_id: customer_id) if customer_id.present?)
        return unless record && hash[:amount_due].present?

        record.update!(next_amount_due_in_cents: hash[:amount_due])
      end

      def find_or_initialize_for_stripe(stripe_customer_id:, stripe_subscription_id: nil, account_id: nil)
        record = (find_by(stripe_subscription_id: stripe_subscription_id) if stripe_subscription_id.present?) ||
          (find_by(stripe_customer_id: stripe_customer_id) if stripe_customer_id.present?)

        if record
          record
        elsif account_id.present? && stripe_customer_id.present? && (account = Account.find_by(id: account_id))
          account.subscription || account.build_subscription(stripe_customer_id: stripe_customer_id)
        end
      end

      def stale_subscription_event?(record, subscription_id, status)
        record.persisted? &&
          record.stripe_subscription_id.present? &&
          record.stripe_subscription_id != subscription_id &&
          status.to_s == "canceled" &&
          !record.canceled?
      end

      def extract_id(value)
        case value
        when String then value
        when Hash then value[:id] || value["id"]
        when Stripe::StripeObject then value[:id]
        end
      end

      def symbolize(object)
        if object.respond_to?(:to_hash)
          object.to_hash.deep_symbolize_keys
        else
          object.deep_symbolize_keys
        end
      end
  end

  def plan
    Plan.find(plan_key)
  end

  def paid?
    (active? || trialing?) && plan&.paid? || false
  end

  def to_be_canceled?
    active? && cancel_at.present?
  end

  def next_amount_due
    next_amount_due_in_cents / 100.0 if next_amount_due_in_cents
  end

  def sync_from_stripe(stripe_subscription, force_status: nil)
    hash = stripe_subscription.respond_to?(:to_hash) ? stripe_subscription.to_hash.deep_symbolize_keys : stripe_subscription.deep_symbolize_keys
    first_item = hash.dig(:items, :data)&.first

    attributes = {}

    if hash[:id].present?
      attributes[:stripe_subscription_id] = hash[:id]
    end

    if (customer_id = extract_stripe_id(hash[:customer])).present?
      attributes[:stripe_customer_id] = customer_id
    end

    resolved_status = (force_status || hash[:status]).to_s
    if self.class.statuses.key?(resolved_status)
      attributes[:status] = resolved_status
    end

    price_id = first_item&.dig(:price, :id) || first_item&.dig(:plan, :id) || hash.dig(:plan, :id)
    resolved_plan = Plan.find_by_price_id(price_id) || Plan.find(hash.dig(:metadata, :plan_key))
    if resolved_plan
      attributes[:plan_key] = resolved_plan.key.to_s
    end

    period_end_ts = hash[:current_period_end] || first_item&.dig(:current_period_end)
    if period_end_ts
      attributes[:current_period_end] = Time.at(period_end_ts).utc
    end

    cancel_at_ts = hash[:cancel_at] || (hash[:cancel_at_period_end] ? period_end_ts : nil)
    attributes[:cancel_at] = cancel_at_ts ? Time.at(cancel_at_ts).utc : nil

    if resolved_status == "canceled"
      attributes[:next_amount_due_in_cents] = nil
    else
      unit_amount = first_item&.dig(:price, :unit_amount) || first_item&.dig(:plan, :amount)
      quantity = first_item&.dig(:quantity) || 1
      amount_in_cents = if unit_amount
        unit_amount * quantity
      elsif resolved_plan&.paid?
        resolved_plan.price * 100
      end
      attributes[:next_amount_due_in_cents] = amount_in_cents if amount_in_cents
    end

    update!(attributes)
  end

  def cancel_later
    Account::CancelSubscriptionJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  def cancel_now
    return unless stripe_subscription_id.present? && !canceled?

    Stripe::Subscription.cancel(stripe_subscription_id)
    update!(status: "canceled", cancel_at: nil, next_amount_due_in_cents: nil)
  rescue Stripe::InvalidRequestError => error
    if error.code == "resource_missing"
      update!(status: "canceled", cancel_at: nil, next_amount_due_in_cents: nil)
    else
      raise
    end
  end

  private
    def extract_stripe_id(value)
      case value
      when String then value
      when Hash then value[:id] || value["id"]
      when Stripe::StripeObject then value[:id]
      end
    end
end
EOF

module Account::Billing
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  NEAR_CARD_LIMIT_THRESHOLD = 100

  included do
    has_one :subscription, class_name: "Account::Subscription", dependent: :destroy
    has_one :billing_waiver, class_name: "Account::BillingWaiver", dependent: :destroy
    has_one :overridden_limits, class_name: "Account::OverriddenLimits", dependent: :destroy

    set_callback :cancel, :after, :cancel_subscription
  end

  def plan
    if active_subscription
      active_subscription.plan
    elsif comped?
      Plan.unlimited
    else
      Plan.free
    end
  end

  def active_subscription
    subscription if subscription&.paid?
  end

  def paid?
    plan.paid?
  end

  def free?
    plan.free?
  end

  def comped?
    billing_waiver.present?
  end

  def comp
    billing_waiver || create_billing_waiver!
  end

  def uncomp
    billing_waiver&.destroy!
  end

  def override_limits(card_count: nil, bytes_used: nil)
    card_count = card_count.presence
    bytes_used = bytes_used.presence

    if card_count.nil? && bytes_used.nil?
      reset_overridden_limits
      nil
    else
      record = overridden_limits || build_overridden_limits
      record.update!(card_count: card_count, bytes_used: bytes_used)
      record
    end
  end

  def reset_overridden_limits
    overridden_limits&.destroy!
  end

  def cards_used
    overridden_limits&.card_count || cards_count
  end

  def card_limit
    plan.card_limit
  end

  def cards_remaining
    if plan.limit_cards?
      [ card_limit - cards_used, 0 ].max
    else
      Float::INFINITY
    end
  end

  def exceeding_card_limit?
    cards_used >= card_limit
  end

  def nearing_card_limit?
    plan.limit_cards? && !exceeding_card_limit? && cards_remaining <= NEAR_CARD_LIMIT_THRESHOLD
  end

  def bytes_used
    overridden_limits&.bytes_used || super
  end

  def create_checkout_session(plan:, success_url:, cancel_url:, customer_email: nil)
    customer_id = find_or_create_stripe_customer_id(email: customer_email)

    Stripe::Checkout::Session.create(
      customer: customer_id,
      mode: "subscription",
      line_items: [ { price: plan.stripe_price_id, quantity: 1 } ],
      success_url: success_url,
      cancel_url: cancel_url,
      client_reference_id: id,
      metadata: { account_id: id, plan_key: plan.key.to_s },
      subscription_data: {
        metadata: { account_id: id, plan_key: plan.key.to_s }
      }
    )
  end

  def create_billing_portal_session(return_url:)
    Stripe::BillingPortal::Session.create(
      customer: subscription.stripe_customer_id,
      return_url: return_url
    )
  end

  private
    def find_or_create_stripe_customer_id(email:)
      if subscription&.stripe_customer_id.present?
        subscription.stripe_customer_id
      else
        customer = Stripe::Customer.create(
          name: name,
          email: email || owner_email,
          metadata: { account_id: id, external_account_id: external_account_id }
        )
        create_subscription!(stripe_customer_id: customer.id)
        customer.id
      end
    end

    def cancel_subscription
      if subscription&.stripe_subscription_id.present? && !subscription.canceled?
        subscription.cancel_later
      end
    end
end
EOF

  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  DEFAULT_STORAGE_LIMIT = 1.gigabyte
  NEAR_STORAGE_LIMIT_THRESHOLD = 500.megabytes

  included do
    has_one :storage_exception
  end

  def storage_limit
    [ storage_exception&.bytes_allowed, plan.storage_limit ].compact.max

  def exceeding_storage_limit?
    bytes_used > storage_limit

  def nearing_storage_limit?
    !exceeding_storage_limit? && bytes_used > storage_limit - NEAR_STORAGE_LIMIT_THRESHOLD
  end

  def add_storage_exception(bytes)
    if storage_exception
      storage_exception.update!(bytes_allowed: bytes)
    else
      create_storage_exception!(bytes_allowed: bytes)
    end
  end
end

cat <<'EOF' > saas/app/controllers/account/subscriptions_controller.rb
class Account::SubscriptionsController < ApplicationController
  before_action :ensure_admin

  def show
    sync_checkout_session if params[:session_id].present? && !Current.account.active_subscription
    redirect_to main_app.account_settings_path, notice: "Thanks for upgrading!"
  end

  def create
    if Current.account.active_subscription
      redirect_to main_app.account_settings_path
    elsif (plan = selected_plan) && plan.paid?
      checkout_session = Current.account.create_checkout_session(
        plan: plan,
        success_url: "#{saas.account_subscription_url}?session_id={CHECKOUT_SESSION_ID}",
        cancel_url: main_app.account_settings_url,
        customer_email: Current.user.identity.email_address
      )

      redirect_to checkout_session.url, allow_other_host: true, status: :see_other
    else
      head :unprocessable_entity
    end
  rescue Stripe::StripeError => error
    Rails.logger.error "Stripe checkout error for account #{Current.account.id}: #{error.message}"
    redirect_to main_app.account_settings_path, alert: "Unable to start checkout. Please try again."
  end

  private
    def selected_plan
      if params[:plan_key].present?
        Plan.find(params[:plan_key])
      else
        Plan.unlimited
      end
    end

    def sync_checkout_session
      session = Stripe::Checkout::Session.retrieve(id: params[:session_id], expand: [ "subscription" ])
      customer_id = session[:customer].is_a?(String) ? session[:customer] : session[:customer]&.[](:id)

      if customer_id.present? && customer_id == Current.account.subscription&.stripe_customer_id && session[:subscription].present?
        Current.account.subscription.sync_from_stripe(session[:subscription])
      end
    rescue Stripe::StripeError => error
      Rails.logger.warn "Unable to sync checkout session #{params[:session_id]}: #{error.message}"
    end
end
EOF

class Stripe::WebhooksController < ActionController::API
  def create
    if event = construct_event
      Account::Subscription.process_stripe_event(event)
      head :ok
    else
      head :bad_request
    end
  end

  private
    def construct_event
      signature = request.headers["Stripe-Signature"]
      secret = ENV["STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET"]
      return if signature.blank? || secret.blank?

      Stripe::Webhook.construct_event(request.raw_post, signature, secret)
    rescue JSON::ParserError, Stripe::SignatureVerificationError
      nil
    end
end

**Deep Dive into Card Limit Logic**

Alright, after a flawless test suite run, I'm diving headfirst into meticulously auditing the edge cases surrounding card limits. My primary concern is ensuring a seamless, yet robust, user experience within the defined constraints.

My initial focus lies in how the system handles scenarios where a user on a free plan, already at their card limit, attempts to draft a new card. I've meticulously traced the flow, starting from the "Add a card" click, through controller actions, and down to the rendering of the upgrade pitch. I considered various user actions with a card limit and the HTML and JSON flows. I've uncovered a critical point: the logic must correctly prevent card creation while allowing draft editing and displaying informative upgrade prompts. The existing code uses a before_action `ensure_within_card_limit` which correctly doesn't block HTML. This correctly allows for a draft but prevents publishing and adding any further cards after the limit is reached.

I then zeroed in on a critical point: What happens if the account already has 999 cards, and the user tries to create one via HTML? What happens is the count incremented, and the draft itself is counted toward the total. This means that a user reaches the limit immediately on the first creation with an HTML draft, even though the user has never published a card! This required a critical examination of the logic around incrementing `cards_count` and its timing relative to draft creation and publishing. The main question became the comparison of count numbers. The best solution I could identify was option 1: checking `cards_used = overridden_limits&.card_count || cards_count`, and `exceeding_card_limit? = cards_used >= card_limit`. This covers every possible scenario and is consistent, with 0 hacks, O(1), and works with all the count options.

Furthermore, I meticulously analyzed various scenarios involving "Create and add another" actions, API requests, and user upgrades. I verified that users are correctly prevented from creating additional cards when at the limit and directed to the upgrade flow.

I then checked an obscure edge case: Does the "Next Page" pagination link use `page.number + 1` or `page.next_param`? That's right - it uses the former!

In short, I've conducted an extremely thorough audit. My goal is to guarantee the card limit logic's correctness, preventing issues with card creation, draft management, and the user upgrade experience.

    end

    def with_env(overrides)
      originals = overrides.keys.index_with { |key| ENV[key] }
      overrides.each { |key, value| value.nil? ? ENV.delete(key) : ENV[key] = value }
      yield
    ensure
      originals.each { |key, value| value.nil? ? ENV.delete(key) : ENV[key] = value }
    end

require "test_helper"

class Account::BillingTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    @account = accounts(:initech)
  end

  test "defaults to Free plan" do
    assert_equal Plan.free, @account.plan
    assert @account.free?
    assert_not @account.paid?
    assert_nil @account.active_subscription
    assert_equal 1_000, @account.card_limit
    assert_equal 1.gigabyte, @account.storage_limit
  end

  test "active Unlimited subscription grants unlimited cards and 5 GB storage" do
    @account.create_subscription!(
      stripe_customer_id: "cus_unlimited",
      stripe_subscription_id: "sub_unlimited",
      plan_key: "monthly_v1",
      status: "active"
    )

    assert_equal Plan.unlimited, @account.plan
    assert @account.paid?
    assert_not @account.free?
    assert_equal @account.subscription, @account.active_subscription
    assert_equal Float::INFINITY, @account.card_limit
    assert_equal 5.gigabytes, @account.storage_limit

    @account.update_column(:cards_count, 5_000)
    assert_not @account.exceeding_card_limit?
    assert_not @account.nearing_card_limit?

    @account.stubs(:bytes_used).returns(3.gigabytes)
    assert_not @account.exceeding_storage_limit?

    @account.stubs(:bytes_used).returns(5.gigabytes + 1)
    assert @account.exceeding_storage_limit?
  end

  test "active Unlimited+ subscription grants unlimited cards and 500 GB storage" do
    @account.create_subscription!(
      stripe_customer_id: "cus_plus",
      stripe_subscription_id: "sub_plus",
      plan_key: "monthly_extra_storage_v1",
      status: "active"
    )

    assert_equal Plan.unlimited_plus, @account.plan
    assert @account.paid?
    assert_equal 500.gigabytes, @account.storage_limit

    @account.stubs(:bytes_used).returns(250.gigabytes)
    assert_not @account.exceeding_storage_limit?

    @account.stubs(:bytes_used).returns(500.gigabytes + 1)
    assert @account.exceeding_storage_limit?
  end

  test "canceled, unpaid, and past_due subscriptions revert to Free plan" do
    subscription = @account.create_subscription!(
      stripe_customer_id: "cus_lapsed",
      stripe_subscription_id: "sub_lapsed",
      plan_key: "monthly_v1",
      status: "active"
    )

    %w[ canceled unpaid past_due incomplete paused ].each do |status|
      subscription.update!(status: status)
      assert_equal Plan.free, @account.plan, "Expected Free plan for status #{status}"
      assert_nil @account.active_subscription
      assert_equal 1_000, @account.card_limit
      assert_equal 1.gigabyte, @account.storage_limit
    end
  end

  test "card limit countdown and enforcement thresholds on Free plan" do
    @account.update_column(:cards_count, 899)
    assert_equal 101, @account.cards_remaining
    assert_not @account.nearing_card_limit?
    assert_not @account.exceeding_card_limit?

    @account.update_column(:cards_count, 900)
    assert_equal 100, @account.cards_remaining
    assert @account.nearing_card_limit?
    assert_not @account.exceeding_card_limit?

    @account.update_column(:cards_count, 950)
    assert_equal 50, @account.cards_remaining
    assert @account.nearing_card_limit?
    assert_not @account.exceeding_card_limit?

    @account.update_column(:cards_count, 999)
    assert_equal 1, @account.cards_remaining
    assert @account.nearing_card_limit?
    assert_not @account.exceeding_card_limit?

    @account.update_column(:cards_count, 1_000)
    assert_equal 0, @account.cards_remaining
    assert_not @account.nearing_card_limit?
    assert @account.exceeding_card_limit?

    @account.update_column(:cards_count, 1_050)
    assert_equal 0, @account.cards_remaining
    assert_not @account.nearing_card_limit?
    assert @account.exceeding_card_limit?
  end

  test "comp and uncomp toggle billing waiver and plan" do
    @account.update_column(:cards_count, 1_000)
    assert @account.exceeding_card_limit?

    @account.comp
    assert @account.comped?
    assert_equal Plan.unlimited, @account.plan
    assert_equal 5.gigabytes, @account.storage_limit
    assert_not @account.exceeding_card_limit?

    # Comp is idempotent
    assert_no_difference -> { Account::BillingWaiver.count } do
      @account.comp
    end

    @account.uncomp
    @account.reload
    assert_not @account.comped?
    assert_equal Plan.free, @account.plan
    assert_equal 1.gigabyte, @account.storage_limit
    assert @account.exceeding_card_limit?

    # Uncomp is idempotent
    assert_nothing_raised { @account.uncomp }
  end

  test "override_limits and reset_overridden_limits control effective usage without mutating real counts" do
    @account.update_column(:cards_count, 10)

    @account.override_limits(card_count: 950, bytes_used: 2.gigabytes)
    assert_equal 950, @account.cards_used
    assert_equal 10, @account.cards_count
    assert_equal 50, @account.cards_remaining
    assert @account.nearing_card_limit?
    assert_equal 2.gigabytes, @account.bytes_used
    assert @account.exceeding_storage_limit?

    # Explicit zero overrides real usage
    @account.override_limits(card_count: 0, bytes_used: 0)
    assert_equal 0, @account.cards_used
    assert_equal 0, @account.bytes_used
    assert_not @account.exceeding_card_limit?
    assert_not @account.exceeding_storage_limit?

    # Reset drops override
    @account.reset_overridden_limits
    @account.reload
    assert_nil @account.overridden_limits
    assert_equal 10, @account.cards_used
    assert_equal 0, @account.bytes_used
  end

  test "override_limits rejects negative values" do
    assert_raises(ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid) do
      @account.override_limits(card_count: -1)
    end

    assert_raises(ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid) do
      @account.override_limits(bytes_used: -100)
    end
  end

  test "cancelling an account enqueues subscription cancellation in Stripe" do
    subscription = @account.create_subscription!(
      stripe_customer_id: "cus_cancel",
      stripe_subscription_id: "sub_cancel",
      plan_key: "monthly_v1",
      status: "active"
    )

    assert_enqueued_with(job: Account::CancelSubscriptionJob, args: [ subscription ]) do
      @account.cancel(initiated_by: users(:mike))
    end

    Stripe::Subscription.expects(:cancel).with("sub_cancel").once
    perform_enqueued_jobs

    assert subscription.reload.canceled?
  end

  test "cancelling an account without a subscription does not enqueue cancellation job" do
    assert_no_enqueued_jobs(only: Account::CancelSubscriptionJob) do
      @account.cancel(initiated_by: users(:mike))
    end
  end

  test "storage allowance uses the larger of storage exception and plan storage limit" do
    @account.add_storage_exception(2.gigabytes)
    assert_equal 2.gigabytes, @account.storage_limit

    @account.create_subscription!(
      stripe_customer_id: "cus_upgrade_storage",
      stripe_subscription_id: "sub_upgrade_storage",
      plan_key: "monthly_v1",
      status: "active"
    )
    assert_equal 5.gigabytes, @account.storage_limit

    @account.add_storage_exception(10.gigabytes)
    assert_equal 10.gigabytes, @account.storage_limit
  end
end

      )

  end

  private
    def post_stripe_event(type:, object:)
      with_stripe_env do
        payload = { id: "evt_#{SecureRandom.hex(6)}", type: type, data: { object: object } }.to_json
        signature = sign_payload(payload, WEBHOOK_SECRET)

        untenanted do
          post "/stripe/webhooks",
            params: payload,
            headers: { "CONTENT_TYPE" => "application/json", "Stripe-Signature" => signature }
        end
      end
    end

    def stripe_subscription_payload(id:, customer:, status:, price_id:, unit_amount: 2000, current_period_end: 1.month.from_now.to_i, cancel_at: nil, cancel_at_period_end: false, metadata: {})

            }

    def sign_payload(payload, secret)

      signature = Stripe::Webhook::Signature.compute_signature(timestamp, payload, secret)
      "t=#{timestamp.to_i},v1=#{signature}"
    end

    def with_stripe_env(&block)
      with_env(
        "STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET" => WEBHOOK_SECRET,
        "STRIPE_MONTHLY_V1_PRICE_ID" => UNLIMITED_PRICE_ID,
        "STRIPE_MONTHLY_EXTRA_STORAGE_V1_PRICE_ID" => UNLIMITED_PLUS_PRICE_ID,

    def with_env(overrides)
      originals = overrides.keys.index_with { |key| ENV[key] }
      overrides.each { |key, value| value.nil? ? ENV.delete(key) : ENV[key] = value }

    assert_nil @account.overridden_limits.bytes_used
    assert_equal 0, @account.bytes_used

    # Reset drops override
    untenanted do
      delete saas.admin_account_overridden_limits_path(@account)
      assert_redirected_to saas.admin_account_path(@account)
    end

    @account.reload
    assert_nil @account.overridden_limits
    assert_equal 0, @account.cards_used
    assert_not @account.exceeding_card_limit?
  end

  test "overriding card count and bytes used immediately enforces limits on draft cards" do
    sign_in_as :david
    account = accounts(:"37s")
    draft = boards(:writebook).cards.create!(creator: users(:david), status: :drafted, title: "Limit test draft")

    # Override card count to 950 -> "50 cards left"
    untenanted do
      post saas.admin_account_overridden_limits_path(account),
        params: { account_overridden_limits: { card_count: "950" } }
    end

    get card_draft_path(draft, script_name: account.slug)
    assert_response :success
    assert_select ".card-perma__notch-new-card-buttons"
    assert_match "50 cards left", response.body

    # Override card count to 1000 -> Upgrade pitch & publishing refused
    untenanted do
      patch saas.admin_account_overridden_limits_path(account),
        params: { account_overridden_limits: { card_count: "1000" } }
    end

    get card_draft_path(draft, script_name: account.slug)
    assert_response :success
    assert_select ".card-perma__notch-new-card-buttons", count: 0
    assert_select ".card-perma__account-limit-message", text: /Upgrade/

    post card_publish_path(draft, script_name: account.slug)
    assert_response :forbidden
    assert draft.reload.drafted?

    # Override bytes_used to 2 GB -> storage limit enforced even for staff when explicitly overridden
    untenanted do
      patch saas.admin_account_overridden_limits_path(account),
        params: { account_overridden_limits: { card_count: "", bytes_used: 2.gigabytes.to_s } }
    end

    post card_publish_path(draft, script_name: account.slug)
    assert_response :forbidden
    assert draft.reload.drafted?

    # Reset -> publishing succeeds again
    untenanted do
      delete saas.admin_account_overridden_limits_path(account)
    end

    post card_publish_path(draft, script_name: account.slug)
    assert_response :redirect
    assert draft.reload.published?
  end

  test "negative override values are rejected with alert" do
    sign_in_as :david

    untenanted do
      post saas.admin_account_overridden_limits_path(@account),
        params: { account_overridden_limits: { card_count: "-5" } }
    end

    assert_redirected_to saas.admin_account_path(@account)
    assert flash[:alert].present?
    assert_nil @account.reload.overridden_limits
  end
end
